stopLine: Stop on unprovable process identity, guessed phone model, model-based credential merging, user-rename overwrite, device-credential schema drift, public exposure, new heavyweight runtime need, product semantics conflict, force push, release, PR, remote deletion, or external publication. Do not write delivery_integrated before real-phone network switching and the remaining human acceptance are verified.
evidenceRefs: Current product authority and candidate source record the tray-owned service lifecycle, browser-hosted Redline console, one-QR phone-to-computer binding, internal invisible transport selection, and the implementation-candidate boundary. The superseded three-choice pairing UI has been removed; remaining target-phone and target-machine acceptance stays open.

DESKTOP-TRAY-WEB-CONSOLE-001 remains user_confirmed; its 2026-08-29 update keeps QR-only authorization but replaces LAN/stable-name/Tailscale user choices with one pairing QR and software-owned path selection. Automatic download, WebView2, and full native UI remain deferred.

Command scripts are wake or emergency entry points; the tray is the service-lifecycle Owner. Password removal does not open access because every phone request still requires a registered device token. Tailscale remains outside physical mDNS advertising.

Web console, one-primary-QR session API, same-device origin adoption, concurrent one-time migration tickets, newest-rollout selection with cached-source rediscovery and latest-user list preview, runtime identity APIs, tray Owner, packaging, and verification consumers exist in this branch as a candidate. No visible LAN/stable-name/Tailscale QR selector remains; this is still not delivery_integrated.

The target chain is launcher to single tray Owner to identified Node service to browser console, then one QR that binds a phone to the computer, persistent LOCALAPPDATA device identity, and software-owned LAN/stable-name/Tailscale selection and failover.

STA NotifyIcon tray, occupant classification, loopback runtime/shutdown APIs, five-area Redline console, transport discovery, one automatically selected pairing QR, diagnostic-only address details, portable-package identity, and main-thread tray IPC are present in source.
The implementation uses Windows PowerShell STA and WinForms already present on target Windows plus the bundled Node runtime; Electron, WebView2, online update, and new external runtimes are excluded.

Tray owns service lifecycle; runtime/tray receipts and process proof gate replacement; Unknown/Unproven occupants are fail-closed; QR is the only authorization owner and trusted-device schema/location remain unchanged.

Version/build identity comes from packaged metadata; runtime and trusted-device records live in LOCALAPPDATA; install .env retains Host/Port/LAN name but removes legacy password configuration; Redline tokens are project-owned CSS.

Automated checks cover QR-only authorization, one-visible-QR source/API shape, reliable initial-address selection, concurrent migration tickets, repeated-scan and cross-origin identity reuse, Tailscale classification, model-first naming, device editing, routing, latest-user list preview, and duplicate rollouts.

The one-QR invisible-transport candidate is implemented, packaged, and locally verified. Remaining work is human NotifyIcon/menu, real-phone path switching, unknown-occupant comparison, and target-machine acceptance. Public internet, automatic download, WebView2, full native UI, release, and delivery_integrated remain deferred.
Implementation candidate is on branch codex/desktop-tray-redline in E:/work/project/codexPWA using Cursor CLI, without a Task Control shell, force push, PR, or release.
tsc server and web projects completed with no errors.

Vitest: 16 files, 52 tests passed, including one-primary-QR API shape, reliable initial transport fallback order, absence of a user-facing network selector, concurrent one-time migration tickets, newest valid rollout selection, QR-only authorization, phone-model behavior, repeated-scan identity reuse, and cross-origin adoption preserving the device ID and row count.
Server compile and Vite production build completed, including PWA generateSW.

Syntax, package-plan, zip-entry classification, BOM-free JSON interoperability, isolation, Current/Predecessor/StalePid/Unknown, fail-closed unknown-occupant, and isolated Headless tray IPC (ping/status/open/stop/start, same-version wake, shutdown-for-replace mutex release) passed without touching live trusted-device data or stopping the live 8787 service during the isolated suite.

Created release/OpenCodexLink-Windows.zip with dist, dist-server, production node_modules, tray scripts/modules/icon, cmd entries, and build identity; zip checker forbids package-root src/server/.env/trusted-devices.

Zip and extracted root validated; node dist-server started on a random non-8787 port with temp CODEX_PWA_DATA_DIR and HOST=127.0.0.1; /api/health, /api/runtime (no controlToken), and /setup passed; live LOCALAPPDATA unused; tray not started; child PID killed in finally.

The final candidate runs from release/deployed-one-qr-final-20260829-015650/OpenCodexLink with tray PID 16400 and service PID 59892 on build 0.1.0+20260828T175508Z. /api/pairing returned exactly one primary QR at http://192.168.31.181:8787 while retaining three diagnostic address records with no extra QR or URL fields. The management panel showed one QR and no LAN/stable-name/Tailscale selector. A 390px browser used that LAN QR, then automatically migrated the same identity to http://100.83.218.96:8787/ and displayed the task list without a rescan or expired-ticket page. The migration-ticket overwrite found during the first probe was fixed with typed concurrent one-time migration tickets; refreshing a pairing QR now replaces only pairing tickets and cannot cancel an in-flight migration. Temporary verification devices L6up9BokHVOM7CM1, 2IqgDFJ9RJaOCq7t, and bmVyKr602NCgIS73 were removed; all three pre-existing device IDs remain and trusted-devices.json returned to SHA-256 309905AC61C461B5B479CC659B1EA90C93EC665662E57067E48BDDF915495A1C.
